Republican Senator [[Mike Braun]] won his first term in office, defeating Democrat former [[Indiana Superintendent of Public Instruction|state Superintendent of Public Instruction]] [[Jennifer McCormick]]. He succeeded Republican incumbent [[Eric Holcomb]], who was term-limited and could not seek a third consecutive term. Primary elections took place on May 7, 2024, in which Republican [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Mike Braun]], [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former [[Indiana Superintendent of Public Instruction|state Superintendent of Public Instruction]] [[Jennifer McCormick]], and [[Libertarian Party (United States)|Libertarian]] software engineer Donald Rainwater won their respective parties' nominations.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org |archive-date=December 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251224083150/https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |url-status=live }} Braun defeated McCormick with 54.4 percent of the vote in the general election.{{cite news |title=Indiana Governor Election Results 2024: McCormick vs. Braun |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-indiana-governor.html |access-date=November 7, 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=November 5, 2024 |archive-date=November 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241106002514/https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2024/11/05/us/elections/results-indiana-governor.html |url-status=live }} Despite this, McCormick's performance marked a significant improvement from that of [[Woody Myers]] [[2020 Indiana gubernatorial election|four years earlier]].
